assumptions: The index set's guaranteed correction radius bounds what may be corrected.
limits: A hit further from a barcode than that radius is not assigned, which is what keeps a failed run visible.
Index reads only: it does not detect index hopping.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which index did each read come from, and how many cannot be assigned reliably?

description: Assign reads to the index each one came from, and say how many could NOT be assigned reliably — a hit further from a barcode than the set's guaranteed correction radius is not that barcode, and counting it as one is how a demultiplexing report hides a failed run.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

barcodes.description: the index set the reads were tagged with.

metric.description: must match the error model the set was designed under. Values: hamming (Hamming (substitutions)), seqlev (Sequence-Levenshtein (indels)), levenshtein (Levenshtein).

reads.description: the observed index reads to assign.

name: demultiplex_reads

ambiguous.description: reads whose nearest barcode is further than the set can correct — these are NOT that sample

assigned.description: reads assigned within the guaranteed correction radius

hits.description: each read with the barcode it was assigned to and the distance
